Fitness essential for effective policing, says DGP
Amaravati: Physical fitness and mental alertness are crucial for effective policing, DGP Harish Kumar Gupta said, urging police personnel to make sports and fitness an integral part of their professional lives.
He was speaking after inaugurating the first AP State Police Sports and Games Meet-2026 at the APSP 6th Battalion grounds in Mangalagiri on Tuesday. The DGP formally declared the four-day sporting event open by releasing balloons and white pigeons into the air.
Around 1,900 police sports persons representing various police ranges and units across Andhra Pradesh are participating in the competitions.
After receiving the guard of honour from 16 participating teams, Gupta said organising such a large-scale police sports meet at the State level for the first time was a significant milestone for the department.
He said police personnel work long hours, take quick decisions in challenging situations, cope with stress and function as teams. Sports help develop the physical and mental capabilities required to effectively handle such demanding responsibilities, he added.
He also thanked the managements of VIT-AP University and Acharya Nagarjuna University for providing the venues and facilities required for the competitions.
“Compete with confidence, play with discipline, accept victory with humility and defeat with determination.
Above all, uphold the honour of the Andhra Pradesh Police Department,” Gupta told the participating sportspersons.
Additional DGP (law and order) N Madhusudhan Reddy, IGs Ake Ravi Krishna (Eagle chief), B Rajakumari (women and child safety wing), Ch Srikanth (technical services and operations), K V Mohan Rao (sports and welfare), DIGs Anburajan (sports and welfare), R N Ammireddy (administration) and Guntur SP Vakul Jindal, along with several senior police officers and personnel, attended the inaugural programme.
